Incident Record: A regular pitstop was made this afternoon at 3:15 PM in the Tourmaline Desert to service engine trouble.
After local wildlife endured a scuffle, the crew incidentally adopted one Pokémon Egg, now in cargo.
No issues expected with the Egg's acquisition.
It will be relinquished to company or personnel at request.
And a little bonus I picked up for my little girl back home in Orre.
Incident Record: An emergency stop was made this Tuesday at 11:53 PM.
An unidentified railway obstruction has brought the vehicle to a halt.
Suspected fallen tree or other similar debris.
Though currently too dark to investigate, will do so in the morning.
Approx. projected delay: 8 hours.
Friday 9:12 AM: I've identified the aforementioned obstruction, though it baffles me.
Specifically, an entire tree has grown in the middle of the rails.
I do not believe there is any such way that I can clear it alone.
As such, I will be returning to Reborn City to request assistance.
Incident Record: Friday 1:37 PM
In what I can only assume is an elaborate prank, I have failed to return to Reborn City.
As I reversed the train down the same track which I had traveled just yesterday, I found a large portion of the rail to be missing entirely.
The wood beams are scattered haplessly between the trees, and the metal has been contorted, and in some places, is absent entirely.
In light of this, I am unable to move the freight at all, and will be returning to Reborn City on foot.
It should not take more than a day to reach the city, and assuming available resources, repairing the rail could be done in as little as two weeks.
Approx. projected delay: 18 days.
Sunday 8:25 PM:
In the continuing saga of happenstances causing me to question my mental health, I have been unable to follow the track to Reborn City.
The scattered wood and disjointed metal I mentioned before was a dramatic understatement.
Entire segments of the track have been disapparated.
Between the increasingly befuddling thickness of forestry and the baffling apparent deconstruction of the rail, I am unable to return to Reborn.
In response to this distortion, I will follow the track on foot-- the only way in which it is (relatively) navigable, towards the Orre Region.
Though it is a considerable distance to walk, I see no second option.
Approx projected delay: 7 days.
Monday 5:39 PM:
It appears I was hasty in my evaluation of the forward-going rail as 'navigable'.
Though I have ridden this way many times, I find the track going forward to be as distorted as it was going back.
These woods are mocking, with trees so in and out and roundabout such that one feels as if they've gone in circles forever.
It was probably by luck that I stumbled upon this train again after having been lost in my expedition.
I'll continue searching for any sign of orient.
Thursday 7:18 PM: It's now been just about a full week since I was stranded in this forest.
Supplies in the train are diminishing quickly.
I find myself rationing more and I desperately hope to discover a source of berries in the woods.
It seems the Pokémon I obtained as a surprise for my daughter will have to be relegated to a gift of apology instead.
Approx. projected delay: Unknown.
Saturday 1:20 AM:
This nightmarish place knows no logic, and yet I think that by a stroke of luck, I may have found the way.
While searching deep in among the woods, I spotted an opening I did not recogize.
As I followed it down a twisted path, I came to a cave.
The very cave through which the rail traveled!
I recognized the stone, but strangely, I could see no rail.
Tomorrow I will gather what supplies I have left and quit this place once and for all.
Sunday 11:20 PM:
As if to taunt me with a glimpse of hope, I have not been successful in my evacuation.
Though I left early this morning, and searched again through every hour of the day, I was unable to locate the railcave from last night.
At this point, and with as little food as is left in this car, I will likely scarcely be able to make it to Orre alive.
Wednesday 2:47 PM:
To my amazement, I once again found the same cave last night.
To my chagrin, I was unable to traverse it.
Though the rails linger inside the cave, they lead nowhere.
What I knew once as a sensible and one-directional tunnel now twists endlessly.
As if my entire life had been tossed into a kaleidoscope, I was unable to navigate the cave, and in fact, when I did finally find an exit--
It turned out to be the very way in which I entered.
I've returned here for the night.
I will try again tomorrow.
Sunday 3:34 AM:
When even finding the entrance to a cave proves difficult, traversing it appears impossible.
I have gone a precise way for these past few days, tracing my steps exactly.
By now I have reliably found that although the path shifts, it is always through the southeast that I am able to stumble into it.
The inside is maddening alone, however. This will require further expedition.
Wednesday 7:44 PM:
After exploring the cave and its nonsensical passages several times more,
I have reliably found a path to a certain cove within the Railcave, and I plan to relocate my remaining supplies there as I press forward.
I will move forward as swiftly as possible with what little food is left, and my daughter's Pokémon in tow.
For whoever may find this train, know the hardships I have faced.
Know, too, how you might escape these labyrinthine woods.
Should you find the Railcave, remember, the direction the rails move is no clue to traversing it.
But as it may be, while they do not point you in the right direction, that appears to be all the guidance you need.
Good luck, stranger.
This is the captain, signing out.

Captain's Log
Should you read this?
Day unknown.
I've been unsuccessful thus far in navigating this hellish cave.
Despite the rails--
Despite the stone markings I've tried to leave--
Despite carefully recording my passages through this place--
I'm baffled.
Utterly and completely...
I felt relocating here would be a leap towards progress to finding my way home.
Instead I feel I've entrenched myself in the prison of this place.
Continue reading?
Progress has once again teased me with her coy seduction.
In my continual stumbling through the labyrinth, I found nestled into the wall, a door imprinted upon the stone in a glowing light.
Beyond its threshold, a world of glittering, static blue and stars.
I do not know what awaits me in the world.
I do know that I am weak.
I am thin, and exhausted-- physically, mentally, emotionally.
I cannot refuse the chance that this will lead me to safety.
But there is no promise in those jilted lands, and I do not expect to return.
If anyone finds this--
Please apologize to my little girl, Snow, for me.
And her gift-- I would ask someone look after the Pokémon.
I may disappear into this strange dimension, but it need not share my fate.
This is Captain Florence, signing out.
Good night.

I know it's weird, but it's how I've always been.
In particular, the number eight has always held special significance for me.

Charlotte likes to give me a hard time about it.

But the reason I hate the number seven........
I was reminded by something one of the Meteors said........
They mentioned a Lin, right?
I knew a girl named Lin once, back at the Orphanage.
It was a couple years ago.
She was a little girl, just a little younger than Anna........
But she was terrifying.
She took pleasure in finding out others' secrets and extorting them.
Even though she was so young, she always tried to manipulate everyone........
And she was good at it.
And for me, whenever I finally had eight of something, she would always take one.
For instance, I would often write and draw in my notebook, and I had differently-colored pens........
But if I ever got eight pens, she would break one of them.
And she would just walk away laughing.
I know it seems childish, but in a place like that, you don't get your own possessions very often.
And she always had to ruin it.
I was always left with seven, and something broken that couldn't be replaced.
